# Independent audit: outside-support buffered response and effective selectors

Audited source:
`candidate 4f875cf42fc6ba0a`,
Sections 1--6. Result: PASS, with the source's finite-dimensional physical-cone,
facet-constant-speed and contact-budget hypotheses retained. No inside-support
or arbitrary nonconstant-speed extension is inferred.

## 1. Exact inverse and curvature

The supporting loss signs agree with the audited all-status formula. An inside
fiber contributes its whole-fiber loss to B_j plus A(r/b-v)_+; an outside fiber
contributes -A(-r/b-v)_+. The proper coarea S_j>0 makes the inverse onto and
strictly increasing, regardless of the selected supporting branch.

With no inside faces, R_j(xi,r) is jointly concave. Its inverse epigraph is
{(xi,q,r):R_j(xi,r)>=q}, hence convex. The equalized-loss hypograph is the
sublevel constraint sum rho_j R_j^{-1}(xi,ell)<=alpha_i(xi). This is convex
for linear or concave alpha_i, proving the claimed concavity. The reversed
curvature for inside-only, linear-budget data is also correct.

The finite branch formulas retain the same physical xi throughout. Their
actual sign cones cover the physical cone, and uniqueness of the scalar
solution makes the linear forms agree on shared boundaries. For a convex
physical cone, the full-relative-dimensional branch supergradients suffice;
ties are handled by continuity, not by arbitrary extra allocations.

## 2. One separator and the effective allocation identity

The downward response set is a convex cone. Separation from the open positive
orthant gives one nonnegative eta, without assuming closedness. The subsequent
finite-gradient convexification is sound: if the compact convex hull of the
branch sums missed the closed negative polar, strict separation would give a
direction in the closure of the physical cone with every branch sum positive.
Approximation by actual directions contradicts the original response bound.

The allocation consistency is an exact algebraic identity. For each positive
group, with the source's lambda weights,

    w_j T_j
      =sum_b lambda_b theta_jb
                  [S_j+sum_l A_l tau_jlb/b_j]
      =sum_b lambda_b rho_j/B_b
      =kappa rho_j.

Also sum_j w_j=eta. Therefore B_eff=eta/kappa and
w_j/eta=(rho_j/T_j)/B_eff. This proves that the averaged body allocation,
section coefficient and contact-budget coefficient are one consistent dual.
The effective supporting selectors are not separately chosen for those terms.
All mass, covariance, energy and parameter contributions inside alpha_i carry
the same kappa factor.

Fixing inside binary branches underestimates R_j and hence its equalized loss.
Choosing the actual signs at the true threshold makes every row agree there,
so uniqueness gives ell=max_zeta ell^zeta. Thus the existential-inside order
is exact; a common separator across that maximum is not obtained.

## 3. Actual interval calibration and normalization

For three copies of [-1,1], M=6, Sigma=1/3 and source energy E(0)=2. Therefore
the physical invariant buffer is delta=epsilon/3. Reflection of the endpoint
intervals gives their cap sum at least 2 for every slope, while sufficiently
steep slopes attain 2. The own interval gives 1+delta. Hence Q=3+delta,
strictly below the middle atomic depth 4 for the stated range.

Endpoint bases have depth at most their atomic bound 2. The two steep middle
quantiles imply delta(y)>=delta at any other alleged deepest mark, and
 delta(y)=delta sqrt(1-y^2) forces y=0. Thus the criticality and uniqueness
claims are actual all-normal claims, not numerical menu observations.

For r_- =1-h t, r_0=1-h t/2, r_+=1, midpoint compatibility is exact for either
sign of h and small positive t. I independently recomputed

    M_t=6-3h t,  E_t(0)=2-h t,
    E_t/M_t=1/3,
    Sigma'_0=-h/3,  delta'_0=-delta h/2.

The contact budget derivative is consequently alpha'=delta h/2. The loss
functions are R_+=h/2+r-(-r-h)_+ and R_-=h/2+r. Their equalization gives

    ell=(1+delta)h/2              when h>=0,
    ell=(5+4delta)h/6             when h<=0.

Subtracting beta D, with beta=(3+delta)/6 and D=3h, gives
G=-h and G=(delta-4)h/6 respectively. Both threshold branch inequalities
have the stated sign. The strict midpoint-concavity gap is (2+delta)/12.

The continued menu is only a covering upper bound after perturbation; the
source explicitly avoids identifying it with the new global depth. That
qualification is necessary and correct.

## 4. Relation to optimized-parameter continuity

The separate theorem
`candidate b2439018eaa1681d`
provides interior-uniform parameter convergence and uniform buffer convergence.
It removes none of the first-order hypotheses audited here. In particular it
does not imply a bounded parameter jet, linearity of alpha_i, constancy of
facet speeds, or exclusion of inside supporting fibers. A varying parameter
can have a thin boundary layer even under that continuity topology.

The precise legitimate upper/lower optimized-value comparisons, including an
exact logarithmic collar term, are saved in
`candidate c72585e587868cec`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
